cruise_provenance.title: Cruise Performance
cruise_provenance.conditions: 2500 Pounds, Recommended Lean Mixture, Cowl Flaps Closed
notes: For best fuel economy at 75% power or less, operate at the leanest mixture that results in smooth engine operation or at peak EGT if an EGT indicator is installed.
cruise_provenance.note: Figure 5-7, Sheets 1 to 4 carried (2000, 4000, 6000 and 8000 ft, printed 5-17 to 5-20); Sheet 5 (10,000 ft) and Sheet 6 (12,000 ft) held, and the 8000 ft / 2100 RPM block held (held_parts). 2500 lb only: the figure prints no other weight. Each sheet is one half of a two-page spread, clipped on its own (clip in the page's displayed frame) and read upright; ocr_args were chosen per sheet by a sweep that ran every candidate setting against the by-eye transcription, and the settings kept are the ones whose read agreed with it completely. Blocks printed '- - -' (the top manifold pressure of some RPM blocks in the 20 C below column) come back absent. Every extracted cell, and every row's oat_c against the temperature its block heading prints, is proven in backlog/evidence/FD-714/takeover/c177/proof_cruise.py (output proof_cruise.txt).

held_parts.part: 8000 ft (Sheet 4, printed 5-20) / 2100 RPM block, 5 rows x 3 blocks
held_parts.why: the page prints the manifold pressures 22, 21, 19, 18, 17 (there is no 20 in. row); extract_cruise_grid infers each block's ladder one inch a row and refuses the sheet on the first label that disagrees, so the sheet is clipped at y 471.5, between the 2200 RPM / 19 in. row and the 2100 RPM / 22 in. row.
held_parts.unblock: backlog/evidence/FD-714/takeover/c177/extract_cruise_mp_ladder.patch (a declared mp_ladders per sheet, checked against every label read); not applied.

held_parts.part: 10,000 ft (Sheet 5, printed 5-21, PDF p45 right page), the whole sheet, 30 rows x 3 blocks
held_parts.why: every RPM block opens at 20.5 in. (then 20, 19, 18, ...). The profile reads only two-digit whole-inch labels, so 20.5 is never a label, and its one-inch inference then files the 20.5 row as 21 in.: a wrong power setting, not a refusal. Held rather than let that through.
held_parts.unblock: the same patch (half-inch labels + declared ladders) AND a cleaner read of PDF p45: with the patch applied to a scratch copy the sheet still refuses on OCR at every setting tried (backlog/evidence/FD-714/takeover/c177/patch_test.txt).

held_parts.part: 12,000 ft (Sheet 6, printed 5-22, PDF p46 left page), the whole sheet
held_parts.why: refused by extract.py's own guards at every one of 64 OCR settings tried (zoom 2.5 to 10, strips 60 to 1000 pt, four clips): 37 on part-read blocks, 11 on the ladder guard, 11 on the column count, 4 on unresolvable ties, 1 on the MP step. On this page Vision splits many fuel-flow decimals into fragments ('7.' and '.3'), leaving 9 to 40 of 84 blocks part-read against a limit of 7, and the misreads it does complete trip the ladder guard, e.g. '12000 ft 2700 RPM ISA+20 gph: 1.7 then 7.1 going DOWN the manifold pressure ladder' where the page prints 7.7 then 7.1. A scratch run with single-cell re-reads enabled on this upright sheet did get through, with ONE WRONG CELL that every guard passed (KTAS 113 for the printed 118 at 2200 RPM / 19 in. / 20 C below: the strip passes filed the 18 in. row's token one row up), which is why the sheet is held rather than tuned further. Never hand-typed.
held_parts.unblock: a better scan of printed page 5-22, or a row check that refuses a reading repeated from the adjacent row; backlog/evidence/FD-714/takeover/c177/proof_cruise.py already holds the by-eye transcription of this sheet to prove any future read against.

held_parts.part: 8000 ft (Sheet 4, printed 5-20) / 2500 RPM / 21 in. / standard temperature (-1 C) block
held_parts.why: OCR did not return this block at the published settings; the page prints 71 %BHP, 125 KTAS, 9.5 GPH. Not hand-typed (BRIEF): it stays absent until a read returns it. Found by the independent review 2026-09-28 (/private/tmp/aircraft-review-1/c177/).

source.doc: Pilot's Operating Handbook, Cessna 1977 Cardinal, Cessna Model 177B (code D1084-13), Section 5 Performance, Figure 5-7 Cruise Performance, printed pages 5-17 to 5-22 = PDF pages 43 (right page) to 46 (left page)
source.note: Scanned handbook with no text layer, bound with a spiral and scanned two book pages to a PDF page (/Rotate 90; the spread reads upright as displayed). Each cruise sheet is one half of a spread, clipped on its own and read upright by macOS Vision OCR (scripts/poh/ocr.py) with sheet-specific ocr_args. extract.py's re-read of a single cell works only on grid-turned sheets, so on these upright sheets a cell Vision misses is dropped with its block, never guessed.

verify_stamp.read: every row re-read from the PDF

engine.doc: Pilot's Operating Handbook, Cessna 1977 Cardinal, Cessna Model 177B, Cessna Aircraft Company, code D1084-13 (1977 model year; the title page prints no issue date and leaves Serial No. blank)
engine.quote: The engine is a Lycoming Model O-360-A1F6D and is rated at 180 horsepower at 2700 RPM.
engine.note: Section 7, ENGINE. Section 2 Power Plant Limitations (2-5, PDF p11) prints 'Engine Manufacturer: Avco Lycoming.' and 'Engine Model Number: O-360-A1F6D.', as does Section 1 Descriptive Data (1-3, PDF p5). The equipment list (6-16, PDF p57) prints 'ENGINE, LYCOMING 0-360-A1F6D' with a ZERO glyph in its line-printer face (checked at zoom 12 against the list's letter O and its zeros), so it is not the quote. No 'NNN HP' token: the book prints '180 horsepower' / '180 BHP', which module_lint.rated_hp() does not parse; the publish should add c177: 180 to module_lint.KNOWN_RATED_HP (cite 2-5 'Maximum Power: 180 BHP.') or the FD-415 BSFC check stops covering c177.

form_schema.doc: Pilot's Operating Handbook, Cessna 1977 Cardinal, Cessna Model 177B, Cessna Aircraft Company, code D1084-13 (1977 model year; the title page prints no issue date and leaves Serial No. blank)
form_schema.quote: CRUISE PERFORMANCE PRESSURE ALTITUDE 8000 FEET (Figure 5-7, Sheet 4 of 6), RPM column: 2700, 2600, 2500, 2400, 2300, 2200, 2100
form_schema.note: Figure 5-7 is keyed by RPM and manifold pressure and prints % BHP, KTAS and GPH per temperature block; 'rpm' is the type the Cessna constant-speed modules already use over rows that carry rpm and mp_inhg (c182t: rpm 2000-2400). Sheets 1-3 (2000-6000 ft) print 2500 to 2100 RPM only; 2600 and 2700 RPM start at 8000 ft, as the tachometer's stepped green arc says (7-17: 'a normal operating range (stepped green arc) of 2100 to 2700 RPM with a step at the 2500 RPM indicator mark. The normal operating range upper limit is 2500 RPM at sea level and increases to 2700 RPM at 8000 feet.'). The carried table (specs/c177.json) holds 2100-2500 RPM at 2000-6000 ft and 2200-2700 RPM at 8000 ft, so 2600-2700 RPM below 8000 ft is off the table. step 100 is the form's increment, not a handbook figure.
